correctness.rationale: The frozen Finding and proof pass at all three stated thresholds. The separate frozen Limitations assertion that two shore components persist at every positive threshold is false: m=n-2 has 2n isolated vertices, and m>n-2 has no vertices. The complete replacement in /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md corrects this for the final claim. Sharing an open neighbor precludes mixed shores, and the union of excluded indices on one shore has size |S| plus the run count. At t=3 only cyclic edges survive. At t=4 each consecutive triple collapses with its distinct length-two diagonal; the remaining graph contains C_n, and a spanning tree containing all but one of its edges shows the cycle represents a primitive generator. At t=5 the excluded triples have positive cyclic gaps after removing one additional unselected vertex from each gap; the circular count is (n/3) binom(n-4,2). Each consecutive four-block collapses with the face {i,i+1,i+3}: the large gap n-3 is the unique possible exterior gap for a four-block. Before collapsing, triangles with a cyclic edge replace each chord by a cyclic path, and the fan at 0 fills the cycle. The resulting simply connected 2-complex has reduced Euler characteristic q_n and free H_2; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the stated integral wedge. The target H_1 is zero and each shore stays connected throughout these three stages, giving the stated maps.

value.rationale: This is a natural controlled perturbation of a complete bipartite graph and an exact deterministic test case for a multineighbor filtration. Three consecutive levels exhibit a primitive old class surviving alongside new loops, their joint disappearance at the next level, and a new second-homology contribution. Integral homotopy types and the specified maps supply more than three isolated numerical Betti counts. The correction restricts the component interpretation without reducing this contribution.
residual_risks: No value is premised on a full persistence barcode or arbitrary 2-factor deletions.
